us_races.note: race-level US midterm rows (usmid_races_ledger.csv); dual instruments scored per race

skill_model_vs_market_us_races.note: edge > 0 means the structural model beats the market on identical questions

research.note: M_research (LLM research-forecaster) scored on calibrated p_research; same questions may also appear under india/world via their own instruments - each instrument answers for itself

matches.note: three-way Brier, scale 0-2 (uniform ref 0.667); never pooled with binary

matches_skill_model_vs_market.note: 3-way Brier (0-2 scale) on identical matches; edge > 0 means the model beats the de-vigged market

calibration_meta.match_events_note: 30 resolved football matches x 3 outcomes (H/D/A), binary events for calibration only
calibration_meta.revisions: latest run per (forecast_id, question) is scored; a re-run supersedes by timestamp (same rule as the ledger and the app)
calibration_meta.voids: VOID resolutions (e.g. a curtailed season with no official champion) are excluded and logged; WATCH rows ARE scored
calibration_meta.note: overall_binary Brier is the 202-row binary cohort; the calibration table pools those 202 plus the 90 football match-outcome events, 292 in all - the football events never enter the binary Brier means (different scale), only the calibration audit

skill_model_vs_market.note: edge > 0 means the structural model beats the market on identical questions
skill_model_vs_market.research_note: common-subset Briers: all three instruments on identical resolved questions

notes: Every resolved pre-registered probability is scored - WATCH rows included. Hit-rate on CALLs alone is gameable by abstention; this table is not.
Binary Brier: 0 perfect, 0.25 = always saying 50%, 1 = certain and wrong. Log scores use p clipped at 1e-4.
Latest run per question is the scored row (re-runs supersede by timestamp, same rule as the ledger).

correlation.formula: error_i = p_i - outcome (outcome in {0,1}); 'backed the wrong winner' = p_i on the wrong side of 0.5. Co-miss = P(both wrong), baseline = P(M2 wrong) x P(M3 wrong) under independence. error_corr is the Pearson correlation of the signed residuals (carries a common-mode floor from sharing the realized outcome - the very risk being measured).
correlation.note: Measured on every resolved question where both instruments forecast. The directional co-miss has a matched independence baseline; we do not report a raw same-sign rate because for binary outcomes it is mechanical.
